info.title: Simba API
info.description:
The HTTP API between Simba's web page and its backend. Built from docs/contracts.md § 6, § 9 and § 10 — if this file and the contract disagree, fix one of them in the same change. POST /api/chat answers with Server-Sent Events (SSE): a long-lived text/event-stream response made of blocks `event: <name>
data: <json>

`. OpenAPI can't express an event stream natively, so the `SseEvent` schema lists every event and its `data` shape, and `x-sse-events` on that response gives the order. The spec is checked in CI by backend/tests/test_api_spec.py (valid OpenAPI, and the same paths and methods as the real FastAPI app).

servers.description: Local backend (uvicorn simba.api:app). The Vite dev server on :5173 proxies /api here.

tags.name: chat
tags.description: Send a message and stream Simba's work and answer.

tags.name: chats
tags.description: The sidebar's chat list: list, create, open, rename, delete.

get.description: Answers without touching the graph or storage.

post.summary: Send one message; stream the turn back as SSE
post.description: Runs one turn of the graph (before_model → agent → after_model, or → refuse). `chat_id: null` starts a new chat titled from this message; a known id continues that chat and moves it to the top; an unknown id is refused with 404 before any streaming, so client text never becomes a database key. Each turn's run (prompt, trace lines, totals or error) is saved with the chat, even if the client disconnects mid-answer.

200.description: The turn as a stream of SSE blocks. Order: `start` (once, first) → `trace` (one per hook point/node) and `token` (answer chunks sent only after after_model approves the complete reply) → `replace` (only if after_model retracted the buffered answer) → `done` (once, last). On an exception after `start`, `error` replaces `done` and ends the stream.
Every chat, ordered by `updated_at` descending (ties: most recently created first).

post.description: The web page doesn't use this — it lets POST /api/chat create the chat on its first message — but the endpoint exists for tools and tests.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: The chat's id (uuid4 hex), from `start` or from GET /api/chats.

get.summary: Open one chat: its messages and its trace runs

200.description: The chat, its conversation (user and assistant messages only, from the checkpointer) and one run per turn, oldest first.

delete.summary: Delete a chat, its runs and its saved conversation

204.description: Deleted. The checkpointer thread is removed first, then the chat row and its runs.

ValidationError.description: The request body didn't match its schema (FastAPI's standard validation error).

message.description: What the user typed. The guard refuses anything over 1,000 characters (a `trace` + fixed reply, not an HTTP error).

chat_id.description: The chat this continues; null starts a new chat.

title.description: Trimmed; blank or missing → "New chat"; over 80 characters after trimming → 422.
Trimmed; must be 1–80 characters after trimming, else 422.

Chat.description: One row in the sidebar. Times are ISO 8601 UTC.

title.description: From the first message (cut to 40 characters + "…"), or a rename.

updated_at.description: Bumped on every new message; the list is sorted by it.

Run.description: One turn's trace block, saved with the chat. Exactly one of `summary` / `error` is set.

prompt.description: The user message that started the turn.

error.description: Why the turn failed, e.g. "interrupted before the reply finished".

TraceStage.description: Which graph node wrote the line (contracts.md § 6). `guard`/`output_guard` are saved before #32 (the hooks redesign); new turns write `before_model`/`after_model`.

TraceStatus.description: ok = passed; blocked = stopped or retracted; error = the node failed; flagged = passed, but the local classifier raised a flag (⚑) for the agent to weigh.

TraceLine.description: One line in the trace panel: what one node did (backend: common.emit_trace).

detail.description: One short line, e.g. "safe · \"weekend ideas for Lisbon\"". Never contains the system prompt.

RunSummary.description: A turn's totals, summed from its trace lines.

SseEvent.description: One SSE block from POST /api/chat. `event` is the block's `event:` line; `data` is its JSON `data:` line.

StartEvent.description: First, always: which chat this turn belongs to (a new one if chat_id was null).

TraceEvent.description: One per graph node, as it finishes.

TokenEvent.description: A piece of the answer (only the agent node's text), sent after the complete reply passes after_model. A refusal, which calls no model, arrives as one token with the whole fixed reply.

ReplaceEvent.description: #15: after_model retracted the buffered answer; none of its text was sent to the browser. The page replaces the empty reply bubble with `text`.

examples: I can't share that. Let's talk about something else.

ErrorEvent.description: Something failed after `start`; the stream ends here (no `done`).

DoneEvent.description: Last, on success: the turn's totals.
